result: HGSOC is the most prevalent ovarian carcinoma subtype, treated with cytoreductive surgery and carboplatin/paclitaxel chemotherapy, with approximately 80% of patients experiencing recurrence, platinum resistance, and death.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3 are background statements supported by appropriate citations (Matulonis et al., 2016; Bowtell et al., 2015). These establish the clinical context for the study and are well-documented in the literature.

result: Gains at 8q24 encompassing MYC and PTK2 (FAK) are frequent in HGSOC, with PTK2 gains associated with elevated FAK expression and Y397 phosphorylation.
evaluation: Claims C4-C6 are prior knowledge statements supported by appropriate citations (Gorringe et al., 2010; Kaveh et al., 2016; Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2011; Zhang et al., 2016). These establish the genomic context for the study.

result: KMF cells were isolated from aggressive ID8-IP cells and exhibit genomic gains in murine regions corresponding to human 8q24.2 and 8q24.3, including Kras, Myc, and Ptk2 genes, with low overall mutational burden.
evaluation: Claims C7-C12 describe the generation and genomic characterization of the KMF model. Exome sequencing data (C8, C10) support the identification of specific chromosomal gains, and bioinformatic mapping (C11) links murine to human cytobands. The low mutational burden (C9) is consistent with the sequencing data showing few mutations detected by RNA-seq.

result: In HGSOC patients, PTK2 and MYC gains co-occur in >70% of tumors, with PTK2 copy number linearly proportional to PTK2 mRNA (R²=0.66) and FAK protein (R²=0.61) levels.
evaluation: Claims C13-C15 are supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1C—figure supplement 1. The linear correlations between copy number and expression are statistically significant with reasonable R² values, supporting the functional relevance of PTK2 amplification.

result: Elevated PTK2 mRNA levels and a 36-gene PTK2-associated signature are associated with decreased relapse-free survival in HGSOC patients.
evaluation: Claims C16-C17 are supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with appropriate sample sizes (n=1435 and n=575), statistically significant p-values (p=0.0009 and p=0.0024), and hazard ratios (1.25 and 1.37). The data are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

result: KMF cells exhibit mesenchymal morphology, enhanced 3D colony formation, elevated FAK expression/phosphorylation, decreased E-cadherin/β-catenin, increased ALDH activity, upregulated cell cycle/DNA repair pathways, and >10-fold increased cisplatin resistance compared to ID8 cells.
evaluation: Claims C18-C24 are supported by multiple complementary assays including microscopy (C18), colony formation (C18), immunoblotting (C19), β-catenin reporter assays (C20), ALDEFLUOR assays (C21), RNA-seq (C22-C23), and cytotoxicity assays (C24). The data are internally consistent and shown in Figure 2.

result: FAK pY397 levels remain elevated in HGSOC tumors after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and trend significantly upward in paired pre/post-chemotherapy samples.
evaluation: Claims C25-C26 are supported by immunohistochemical analysis of paired patient samples (n=14) with quantitative image analysis. The paired analysis (C26) showing increased pY397 FAK post-chemotherapy is statistically significant (p<0.05, paired t-test) as shown in Figure 3D.

result: FAK Y397 phosphorylation is restored during OVCAR3 tumorsphere formation (2-3 days) and is increased by low-dose cisplatin treatment along with β-catenin Y142 phosphorylation.
evaluation: Claims C27-C28 are supported by time-course immunoblotting experiments shown in Figure 4B-D. The restoration of FAK pY397 during tumorsphere formation and its increase with cisplatin treatment are clearly demonstrated, supporting non-canonical FAK activation.

result: Low-dose cisplatin increases tumorsphere formation and ALDH activity, while FAK inhibitor reduces these parameters; only the combination of cisplatin and FAKi decreases tumorsphere viability.
evaluation: Claims C29-C31 are supported by complementary assays (tumorsphere formation, ALDEFLUOR, viability) shown in Figure 5A-C. The data demonstrate that FAKi alone is not cytotoxic but synergizes with cisplatin, with appropriate statistical analysis (p<0.05-0.001).

result: Cisplatin-resistant A2780-CP70 and OVCAR10-CP cells acquire dose-dependent sensitivity to FAKi in 3D but not 2D culture, with FAKi preventing colony formation and the combination of FAKi+CP inducing apoptosis.
evaluation: Claims C32-C34 are supported by growth assays, colony formation assays, and apoptosis assays shown in Figure 6. The 3D-specific sensitivity to FAKi is demonstrated by comparing 2D and 3D conditions (Figure 6B and Figure 6B—figure supplement 1), supporting context-dependent FAK dependence.

result: In A2780-CP70 xenografts, single-agent FAKi reduces tumor mass ~40%, with greater reduction when combined with chemotherapy; FAKi+CPT suppresses FAK pY397, reduces ALDH-1A1 staining, and increases apoptosis.
evaluation: Claims C35-C38 are supported by in vivo tumor growth experiments with appropriate controls (n=6 per group) and multiple readouts including tumor mass, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, and TUNEL assays shown in Figure 7. Statistical significance is demonstrated (p<0.05-0.001).

result: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated FAK knockout in KMF and OVCAR3 cells was specific (165 unique variants in KT13), resulted in cisplatin sensitivity, and phenotypes were rescued by FAK re-expression.
evaluation: Claims C39-C42 are supported by CRISPR targeting, exome sequencing validation (C40), cytotoxicity assays (C41), and rescue experiments (C42) shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1. The specificity of CRISPR targeting and rescue experiments provide strong genetic evidence for FAK's role.

result: FAK-WT but not kinase-inactive FAK-R454 is phosphorylated at Y397 in 3D conditions; FAK-WT expression restores elevated ECM proteins, β-catenin, ALDH activity, Myc levels, and cisplatin resistance, while FAK-R454 does not.
evaluation: Claims C43-C46 are supported by immunoblotting (C43), mass spectrometry (C44), ALDEFLUOR assays (C45), and cytotoxicity assays (C46) shown in Figure 8-9. The differential effects of FAK-WT versus FAK-R454 provide strong evidence for kinase activity-dependent functions.

result: Intrinsic FAK kinase activity is essential for KMF tumor establishment in mice, and β-catenin signaling alone is insufficient to support tumor growth in the absence of FAK.
evaluation: Claims C47-C48 are supported by in vivo tumor growth experiments showing FAK KO and FAK-R454 cells fail to establish tumors, while FAK-WT rescues growth (Figure 9D-F). The failure of β-catenin ΔGSK to rescue tumor growth (C48) demonstrates FAK has functions beyond β-catenin activation.

result: Transcriptomic analysis identified 591 FAK activity-dependent genes, 241 co-regulated by FAK and β-catenin, with 135 matching genes elevated in HGSOC including Myc; qRT-PCR validated DNA repair and pluripotency genes elevated by FAK-WT.
evaluation: Claims C49-C54 are supported by RNA-seq with appropriate filtering strategies, KEGG pathway analysis, TCGA comparison, and qRT-PCR validation shown in Figure 10. The multi-step filtering approach and independent validation by qRT-PCR (C54) strengthen the findings, though causality between these transcriptional changes and phenotypes is not established.
